answer: node2vec does not dynamically adjust the walk length l or the context window size k per vertex based on local clustering coefficients during walk generation. In the original node2vec formulation, the walk length and window size are global hyperparameters chosen by the user and kept fixed across vertices. What node2vec does adaptively is the transition bias of the biased random walk procedure (BRWP): at each step, the next node is sampled using parameters p and q to interpolate between breadth-first-search-like and depth-first-search-like exploration. This means the walk generation is guided by the graph structure through second-order transition probabilities, but not by per-vertex clustering coefficients. If one wanted to make walk length or window size depend on local clustering coefficient, that would be a speculative extension rather than part of node2vec itself. In practice, node2vec learns node embeddings from the generated random walks using a skip-gram-style objective, and the fixed window size k determines which nodes in each walk are treated as context for a target node.
